---
title: "Roadmap"
---

This page carries the project timeline — what Kailash has delivered, with the
tracking issue for every step — and the forward plan by release train. Every
delivered item below was completed as a tested, GPG-signed pull request and
verified by execution; the dates are the issue-close dates. Trishula, the
sister project, keeps
[a timeline in the same shape](https://trishula.dev/roadmap.html) — the projects share the build discipline, not the codebase.

## The road so far

### 3 October — baseline

- The product specification (the implementation plan) is written and reviewed before implementation; the [roadmap board](https://github.com/orgs/kailash-os/projects/1) graduates from planning to GitHub as issues KA-01…KA-44 with the label, effort and milestone catalog ([KA-21](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/21), [engineering-agreement sweep](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/46)–[57](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/57), [website issue #1](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-website/issues/1)).
- Repository governance lands on both product repos: merge queue + branch protection ([os#48](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/48)), contributing + security policy ([os#46](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/46)), Renovate ([os#50](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/50)), the hypothesis-first TDD standard ([os#52](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/52)), and the OpenSSF badge pair — Best Practices + Scorecard — in the badge row ([os#53](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/53), [os#55](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/55)).
- Both production repos relicense to BSD-3-Clause ([os#62](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/62), [pkgs#4](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/4)); the website follows ([website#13](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-website/issues/13)).

### 9 October — the OS skeleton builds

- The OS repo revives as a real flake: skeleton tree + convention commits, pinned inputs, explicit unfree posture, no global CUDA, and profiles/minimal.nix evaluating with zero categories enabled ([KA-01](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/1): [118](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/118), [122](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/122), [127](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/127)).
- The overlay repo seeds as an independently consumable flake — the nixpkgs↔NixOS split — and the OS flake.lock pins it at lock-time ([KA-02](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/2): [pkgs#5](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/5), [os#128](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/128)).
- The engineering standard hardens: harness-before-capability ordering, GitHub Actions as the authoritative check surface ([os#120](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/120)), flake-check on hosted runners both repos ([os#129](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/129), [pkgs#8](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/8)), AGENTS.md as the contributor/agent contract ([os#125](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/125), [pkgs#23](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/23)).
- The platform layer formerly named BUILD becomes OPS, O-1…O-7 ([os#121](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/121)); the website's [Build page](https://kailash.site/build.html) opens — the verification loop as a public page.

### 10 October — the taxonomy becomes data

- categories.yaml: the post-purge census locks — CORE + CLASSIC C-1…C-10, ATTACK A-1…A-8, DEFENCE D-1…D-7, OPS O-1…O-7, deliberate exclusions recorded ([KA-04](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/4): [pkgs#6](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/6), [12](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/12), [26](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/26), [14](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/14)).
- tools.yaml: validator invariants committed watched-RED before the data lands; manifest stubs ([KA-05.1](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/15), [KA-02.2](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/10)).
- The first bespoke derivation lands: garak, the LLM vulnerability scanner — nvfetcher pin, Shape-1 derivation, --list-probes smoke; a hosted-runner PEP-517 catch fixed same day ([pkgs#20](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/20), [pkgs#22](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/22)). PyRIT packages ([pkgs#16](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/16)); the kailash CLI core opens — list / search / info over the manifest ([pkgs#17](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/17)).
- CI becomes manifest-driven: the manifest→matrix generator, build.yml in both repos, and the negative gate — a deliberately broken manifest fails the build — merged ([os#130](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/130), [pkgs#18](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/18), [neg gate](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/28)). The OS-to-overlay pin resolves on the real lock ([os#128](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/128)).
- The website [Tools page](https://kailash.site/tools.html) renders the category census from the manifest with provenance and field glossary ([website#26](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-website/issues/26)).

### 11 October — the gates acquire teeth

- Every manifest slot is entered — CLASSIC 142, ATTACK 58, DEFENCE 46, OPS 91, data-packs excluded from counts ([pkgs#30](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/30), [39](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/39), [40](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/40), [36](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/36), [38](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/38)) — and the flagship stack builds green: garak manifest row + smoke, promptfoo (npm-pinned + freshness decision), ART, counterfit ([pkgs#34](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/34), [35](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/35), [31](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/31), [33](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/33)); acceptance smokes joined to the build legs ([pkgs#46](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/46)).
- Safety becomes mechanical: the safety-defaults module ships the §11.2 double-key lab-mode gate (KAILASH_LAB_MODE + host kailash.labMode), the no-auto-start audit and sops-nix secret hygiene ([os#144](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/144), [os#145](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/145)); the generator wraps every safety:exp tool and CI alarms on drift ([os#149](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/149), [pkgs#44](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/44)).
- Profiles ship hardened: redteam-ai (ATTACK full + O-4) and minimal-hardened ([os#146](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/146), [os#148](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/148)).
- Release naming moves to calendar trains — 2026.xx, bare-year reserved for GA — superseding the scheme across every surface ([KA-47](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/47): [os#147](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/147)). The cadence policy + Renovate reconcile against plan §8.5 ([pkgs#29](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/29)); the README category table is generated, never hand-synced ([os#143](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/143)); ADR records start ([os#133](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/133)); the kailash binary cache goes live ([os#138](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/138), [pkgs#41](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/41)).

### 12 October — every category becomes a boot-tested module

- Layer CLASSIC completes C-1…C-10 — exemplar module first per the §4.5 contract, then generated siblings; Burp/ZAP/Caido pinned exact; exploitation software-only; forensics/IR; Runtime AppSec for AI; the SDR pack recorded opt-in, never on default images ([KA-06](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/6) / [KA-07](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/7): [os#155](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/155), [159](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/159), [163](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/163), [164](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/164), [167](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/167), [172](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/172)).
- The platform modules land: O-1 MLOps (mlflow service), O-2 compute & serving (k3s/podman, ollama/llama.cpp), O-5 SDKs, torch via Shape 4 — non-GPU default + explicit -nvidia variant ([os#160](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/160), [161](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/161), [174](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/174), [pkgs#51](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/51)); O-3 vector stores + O-4 local LLM + O-6 authoring + per-category devShells ([os#162](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/162), [165](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/165), [169](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/169), [170](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/170)).
- ATTACK category modules open — A-1 AI recon, A-2 prompt injection, payload data packs, trufflehog cross-list ([os#166](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/166), [os#168](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/168)).
- Layer DEFENCE completes D-1…D-7 — guardrails, evals, provenance, threat modelling, governance, standards — with probe receipts + packaging-reality legs ([os#177](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/177), [pkgs#54](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/54)).
- The VM smoke suite lands boot legs + a contract watchdog ([os#176](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/176)); cross-repo harness defects exposed by the expanded ledger are fixed in the same window ([os#136](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/136), [pkgs#32](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/32)).

### 13 October — the long tail lands, the release train departs

- The ATTACK long tail lands: A-3 agentic/MCP + A-4 supply chain (mcp-inspector, mcp-scan, guarddog, picklescan, modelscan + the novel-probe starter set), and O-7 agent & MCP operability with short-lived human-minted capability grants ([os#179](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/179), [pkgs#55](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/55), [os#182](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/182), [pkgs#56](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/56)).
- A-5…A-8 complete with the mlflow-bypass integration leg — an attack tool exercised against the platform's own lab deployment ([os#185](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/185)); the GVM/OpenVAS service module arrives ([os#180](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/180)); kailash.data.* wordlist/data packs flip opt-in with proof legs ([os#183](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/183), [pkgs#57](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/pull/57)).
- Platform VM acceptance: a booted platform profile completes an ollama prompt and serves MLflow on :5000 ([os#184](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/184)).
- The image matrix ships shape-first: QEMU images primary, ISOs secondary, size budgets enforced ([KA-28](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/28): [os#173](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/173), [os#181](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/181)).
- The first staged cut is engineered: signed tag, release lock bump, changelog, the standing-cut checklist ([KA-46](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/141): [os#196](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/196), [os#195](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/195) path-scopes the build matrix, [os#192](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/192) enables the Renovate dashboard).

### 13 October — 2026.01-alpha.1 ships, provenance attached

- **The first release of the Kailash OS distribution publishes** ([2026.01-alpha.1](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/releases/tag/2026.01-alpha.1)): the full four-layer catalogue on a pinned, reproducible NixOS base — 32 census categories, 337 tool slots (CLASSIC 142, ATTACK 58, DEFENCE 46, OPS 91). The release body carries the gate table: hosted build (37 legs), flake-check, OpenSSF Scorecard, manifest validator at the pin, and the §11.2 refusal contract — the generator refuses the exp-carrying A-8 emit by name ([KA-46](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/141)).
- **Artefacts are born attested**: release-images grants id-token and emits, per artefact, an in-toto SLSA v1.0 build-provenance statement + SPDX SBOM, signed with a Sigstore certificate over the repository's OIDC identity and written to the public Rekor transparency log — before upload, not after ([os#198](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/198), [KA-48](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/171)).
- Image releases attach from hosted runners with artefact-naming + actor checks ([os#197](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/197), [os#199](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/199)); the matrix completeness amendment builds the four never-built targets from the tag's pin and SHA256SUMS covers all 12 §8.1 artefacts ([os#200](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/200)).
- The aarch64 half of the matrix builds natively — x86 hosted, arm local, the split-arch strategy of [ko#198](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/198) — and the aarch64 posture is documented honestly: partial support ([KA-36](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/36)).

### 14 October — the cut completes; the docs estate opens

- Oversized artefacts stay verified: QEMU images above GitHub's per-asset cap publish in chunks, SLSA/attestation intact, with per-leg checksum sheets; the workflow-trigger defect that would have left four targets never-built was found and fixed ([os#207](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/207), [os#202](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/pull/202), [KA-33.4](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/206)).
- The standing release ladder fixes the GA discipline: alpha → rc.1 → GA, the cut checklist, per-criterion verdicts ([KA-49](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/204)).
- The implementation specification goes public in-repo, every §-citation hyperlinked to an anchor ([KA-51](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/209): [docs/spec.md](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/spec.md)) — the citation convention the site enforces.
- **The docs estate opens**: the [Kailash OS Cookbook](https://book.kailash.tools) goes live at book.kailash.tools — task-oriented recipes with real commands and expected output shapes; getting-started, the garak LLM01 prompt-injection exemplar, the attack-then-verify pair and the administrator chapters are live; the scanning and ops lanes continue on the book ([KA-WS-5](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-book/issues/1), [first build](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-book/issues/2)). The [Kailash OS Guide](https://docs.kailash.tools) goes live at docs.kailash.tools — Parts I–IV (taxonomy census, build security & governance, administrator guide) plus the per-category directory generated from the manifest ([KA-WS-6.1](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-guide/issues/2), [directory](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-guide/issues/15)); the per-tool reference-page lane is open ([KA-WS-6](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-guide/issues/1)).

## What ships next

Work is tracked on the [Kailash Roadmap board](https://github.com/orgs/kailash-os/projects/1)
(org Project, one Kanban view) as issues KA-01…KA-51 in the
[`kailash-os`](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os) org: the OS repo, the
[`kailash-packages`](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages) overlay, and the
[`kailash-website`](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-website) site mirror. The board's
*Status* field (not labels) is the record of progress; the
[dependency graph](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/61) is the canon map — planning edges, not enforcement gates. Every
issue lands a runnable artefact with an exit criterion — the distribution is proven by the
checks it ships, not by prose.

## How an item ships

The delivery unit is an hour-scale slice with a watchable RED→GREEN commit pair — hypothesis-first
TDD, [harness-before-capability](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/119) ordering, every commit GPG-signed and merge-gated. The
[Build page](https://kailash.site/build.html) documents the loop; the
[sprint register](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/61) maps every item to the spec sections it implements. Releases follow the
[cadence policy](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/guide/releases.md): a train
every six weeks, alpha → rc.1 → GA, the lockfile is the version, nothing self-updates.

## The docs estate

Three public surfaces carry the specification and the practice, all generated or verified from the
same manifest revision:

- **kailash.site** — this site: the specification overview (taxonomy, architecture, verification
  standards, governance) and the generated [tools](https://kailash.site/tools.html) page.
- **[docs.kailash.tools](https://docs.kailash.tools)** — the Kailash OS Guide: what Kailash is, the
  build's security and governance model ([KA-WS-6](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/208)),
  the per-category directory generated from the manifest, a man-style reference page per tool with the
  exemplar live ([garak(1)](https://docs.kailash.tools/reference/garak.html)) — the manifest-driven
  generator that lands all 321 reference pages is the open lane
  ([KA-WS-6.6](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-guide/issues/17)).
- **[book.kailash.tools](https://book.kailash.tools)** — the Kailash OS Cookbook: task-oriented
  recipes — attack, defence, ops, admin — with real commands and expected output; getting-started,
  the prompt-injection exemplar and the administrator chapter are live, with the recipe directory
  and per-family walkthroughs continuing ([KA-WS-5](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/208)).

## Contributing

Contributions follow the [contributing guide](https://kailash.site/contributing.html) and the
engineering standard in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/AGENTS.md):
add tools via a manifest entry, not hand-edited module files; CI validates, builds and VM-tests every
change; commits and tags are GPG-signed; work happens on leaf branches cut from the default branch.
Pick anything on the [2026.01 completion](https://github.com/orgs/kailash-os/projects/1) or the next
train — the spec section cited in the issue body is the design source. Kailash OS is BSD-3-Clause
(bundled tools keep their upstream licences).
